title: Measure tree height with an explicit empty case
prompt: Return height in nodes: an empty tree has height 0, a leaf 1. Node uniquely owns left and right children. height only borrows a const Node pointer. Input is an acyclic tree with at most 100 levels.
signature: struct Node; std::size_t height(const Node* root)

tests.label: Wide is not tall
tests.hint: Take maximum depth, not number of nodes.

hints: Ask each child for its height.
The parent adds one to the larger child result.
explanation: The null base case ends recursion; each result becomes the answer for one subtree. const prevents changes through the borrowed pointer, while unique_ptr keeps ownership in the tree. The starter returns 1 for every nonempty tree, including the sample of height 3. An iterative breadth-first count of levels is better when extreme depth makes recursion unsafe.
